newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel sending envoy to U.S. with proposals.
newsitem.headline: Israel sending envoy to U.S. with proposals.

text.p: Israeli leader Benjamin Netanyahu said on Monday he was sending a senior adviser to Washington with proposals for ending a four-month-old peacemaking crisis with Palestinians.

"We are working jointly with the Americans and we have some bridging ideas. I believe they're good proposals," a spokesman quoted Netanyahu as telling members of the ruling Likud parliamentary faction.
He did not elaborate on the ideas.

"I have decided to send Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh, who coordinates the Palestinian issue for me, to Washington for meetings with Dennis Ross and others," Netanyahu said. Ross is a special U.S. Middle East envoy.

Israeli-PLO talks, launched with a U.S.-backed interim accord in 1993, have been stuck since Netanyahu started building a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem in March, triggering Palestinian protests.

On Saturday, Palestinian negotiator Saeb Erekat said Washington was preparing a "package deal" of measures to end the deadlock. But Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat said on Sunday there were as yet no new U.S. initiatives.

Netanyahu again demanded on Monday that Arafat's Palestinian Authority investigate allegations that senior security officials sent three police officers, now in Israeli custody, to attack Jews in the West Bank.

On Monday, Palestinian police said they had uncovered ready-to-use explosives and disguises at a West Bank apartment near Bethlehem which they suspect was a bomb lab of the anti-Israeli Hamas movement.

Netanyahu has demanded that Palestinians do more to crack down on Moslem guerrilla groups opposed to Israeli-PLO peace accords. "I would want to see these efforts done continuously," the Israeli leader said.

The Bethlehem area police found Jewish religious skullcaps and prayer shawls and Israeli army uniforms. Suicide bombers and kidnappers have posed as Israelis to carry out attacks that have killed scores of people in Israel.

Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy met top PLO negotiator Nabil Shaath on Sunday as part of a European bid to break the stalemate. Shaath hailed what he called "a real serious and sincere effort to break the impasse".

But negotiators were unable to announce a hoped-for meeting between Levy and Arafat at the 15-member European Union's foreign ministers' meeting in Brussels on Tuesday. It was unclear whether the Palestinian leader would attend.

Israeli opposition leader Ehud Barak flew to Amman on Monday on a surprise visit at the invitation of Jordan's King Hussein, officials said. Jordan has also been looking for ways to break the peacemaking deadlock.

Netanyahu, who has angered the king with his right-wing policies on Jerusalem and Jewish settlements, resists the peace deals that Barak's Labour party signed with Arafat based on the principle of land-for-peace.
